title: Airport and Airway Extension Act of 2018, Part II
official_summary:
Airport and Airway Extension Act of 2018, Part II

(Sec. 2) This bill extends: (1) airport planning and development and noise compatibility planning and programs at increased levels until October 7, 2018; (2) various expiring aviation authorities, including those under the Vision 100-Century of Aviation Reauthorization Act and the FAA Modernization and Reform Act of 2012, through such date; (3) the expenditure authority of the Airport and Airway Trust Fund through October 8, 2018, and (4) excise taxes for such fund through such date.

summary.headline: This law briefly extends federal airport funding, FAA programs, and airport-related taxes until early October 2018.
summary.what_it_does: It is a short-term extension, not a full reauthorization. It keeps airport planning, development, and noise compatibility programs running at increased funding levels until October 7, 2018. It also extends several expiring aviation authorities, including ones from the Vision 100 and FAA Modernization and Reform Act laws, through that same date. In addition, it extends the Airport and Airway Trust Fund's spending authority through October 8, 2018, and the excise taxes that feed the fund.

who_it_affects.how: They can keep receiving federal planning, development, and noise compatibility funding under the extended levels until early October 2018.
The aviation excise taxes that fund the Airport and Airway Trust Fund stay in place through early October 2018, so ticket-related taxes continue to be collected.
Several expiring FAA aviation authorities remain in effect through early October 2018 instead of lapsing.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted September 29, 2018; the extensions run through October 7 or October 8, 2018, depending on the provision.
